newsitem.title: USA: Banks OK interim Marvel cash collateral use.
newsitem.headline: Banks OK interim Marvel cash collateral use.

text.p: Marvel Entertainment Group Inc will be able to use cash collateral to finance operations until a July 10 hearing on a proposed new debtor-in-possession (DIP) financing plan.

Moments prior to a scheduled hearing Tuesday, before U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Helen Balick, Chase Manhattan Corp, agent for prepetition and current DIP lenders, agreed to the interim use of the cash collateral.

In agreeing to the July 10 hearing date, Judge Balick once again scolded both sides. "There is too much litigation in this case; I think in all likelihood that this whole matter is an abuse of the bankruptcy law. Instead of running up attorney's fees and having egos bouncing about out there, you better do some sensible thinking," Balick said.
Last month, a group of Marvel Holdings Inc bondholders, led by investor Carl Icahn, won a prolonged legal battle to take control of the debtor companies from Ronald Perelman.
The banks are owed $100 million for current DIP financing, which is due and payable July 9, and $610 million for prepetition loans.

They object to a proposed replacement DIP financing of $125 million by two of Icahn's limited partnerships because it would bump prepetition lenders from their first lien position into a second lien position.

Chase attorney Chaim Fortgang told Balick "We are not going to object to limited cash collateral usage." But Fortgang added that the banks did not consent to the replacement DIP financing because as a priming loan it would take precedence over the bank's first lien.
